headline: Rest of World reports that AI data centres' demand for memory chips is raising phone prices and making the cheapest smartphones scarce, which could keep poorer people offline.
score_reason: Kept at 5: figures from IDC, Counterpoint, Omdia and GSMA; the link to AI demand rests on analysts' assessments.
importance_line: Buyers outside the US, especially poorer ones, are hit first as handset prices rise (21% in India against 5% in the US), then groups trying to get people online, but the cause rests on analysts' assessments and no estimate is given of how many people will stay offline.
summary: Rest of World reports that a shortage of memory chips, the components that store a phone's data, driven by AI data centres' demand has raised prices of existing smartphone models by about 15% globally this year and of new models by about 25%. Shipments of phones under $100 fell almost 60% in the second quarter, according to IDC; analysts say Chinese makers are dropping cheap models and the shortage will last, and an official at the GSMA Foundation, part of the mobile industry association, warns that unaffordable phones could widen the digital divide.
notes: Read in full. Rest of World's own reporting with analyst and GSMA quotes.
